Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:10:1.english: [Is it] forewarned with regard to people - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:11:1.hebrew: אטרפה - לא קטלינן ליה, דגברא קטילא קטיל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:11:1.english: Regarding a tereifa - We do not execute it, for it killed a [person who is already] dead.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:12:1.english: Is it forewarned to pay - [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:12:2.english: Where it killed and fled to the marsh - After they testified against it, it fled.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:13:1.hebrew: שהוזמו זוממי זוממין - כשנגח ב' נגיחות ראשונות והעידו בו ב' כיתות עדים, באו כת אחת והזימום ופטרוהו. וכשנגח נגיחה שלישית והעידו בו, באתה כת המזמת להזימן, והוזמה אותה הכת אף על הזמות ראשונות, ונמצא השור מועד ומשלם כופר על השלישית:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:13:1.english: Where those who rendered [the witnesses] conspiring witnesses were [themselves] proven to be conspiring witnesses - When [the ox] gored two initial gorings and two sets of witnesses testified against it, one set came and rendered them conspiring witnesses, and [thereby] exempted it. And when it gored a third goring and [witnesses] testified against it, the [same] set that had rendered [the others] conspiring witnesses came to render them conspiring witnesses, and that set was [itself] proven to be conspiring witnesses even regarding the first accusations of conspiracy; thus the ox is found to be forewarned, and [its owner] pays ransom for the third [goring].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:1.hebrew: הניחא אי לייעודי תורא בעינן - ג' ימים דכתיבי בקרא:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:1.english: This works out well if we need to forewarn the ox - [Namely, the] three days that are written in the verse.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:2.hebrew: שפיר - הרי נגח שלש נגיחות בג' ימים, ואע"ג שלא נתקיימה העדאתו אלא בכת אחת, לא איכפת לן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:2.english: It works out well - Behold, it gored three gorings on three days, and even though its forewarning was only upheld through one set [of witnesses], it does not matter to us.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:3.english: But if we need to forewarn the man - [For] three days.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:4.hebrew: אמר לא הוה ידענא - ב' נגיחות הראשונות דאינטריה, שהמזימין הטעוני:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:4.english: He could say: I did not know - [about] the first two gorings that I should have guarded it, because those who rendered [the witnesses] conspiring misled me.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:14:5.english: He was standing by it - For the refuting witnesses testified that he was standing by it and saw its gorings.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:15:1.hebrew: רבינא אמר - משכחת לה דלא נסקל בשתים הראשונות, כגון שהעדים המעידים עליו אין מכירין את השור, ובג' הוכר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:15:1.english: Ravina said - You find [a case] where it was not stoned for the first two [gorings], such as where the witnesses testifying about it do not recognize the ox, and on the third [goring] it was recognized.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:16:1.hebrew: מאי הוה ליה - לבעלים למיעבד, ואמאי מחייבת ליה כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:16:1.english: What could he [have done] - [What could] the owner have done, and why do you obligate him [to pay] ransom?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:17:1.hebrew: לאחר שנגמר דינו - דהכי משמע קרא: משבא שור לידי סקילה, יסקל, ושוב לא יאכל את בשרו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:17:1.english: After its verdict had been reached - For this is what the verse implies: once an ox has come to [be liable to] stoning, it shall be stoned, and henceforth its flesh shall not be eaten.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:20:1.hebrew: להיכא דסקליה מסקל - ואתא "לא יאכל" לאוסרו בהנאה, וכדרבי אבהו. ו"נקי" מבעיא ליה לדרשה אחריתי, לחצי כופר ולדמי ולדות, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:20:1.english: Where they stoned it - And "it shall not be eaten" comes to prohibit it from deriving benefit, in accordance with [the statement of] Rabbi Abbahu. And "innocent" [naki] is needed for another exposition — for half-kofer and for the value of offspring — as [stated] below.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:22:1.hebrew: כדרך שפרט לך בנבילה - שכתב לך בה "לא תאכלו", והוצרך הכתוב לפרש לך בה היתר הנאה — "לגר אשר בשעריך וגו'". אלמא "לא תאכלו" איסור הנאה הוי משמע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:22:1.english: In the manner that it specified for you with regard to an animal carcass - For it wrote for you regarding it, "You shall not eat [any carcass]," and Scripture had to specify for you regarding it permission [to derive] benefit: "To the ger who is in your gates, etc." Thus, "You shall not eat" implies a prohibition against [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:1.hebrew: ה"מ - דמפיק קרא לאיסור הנאה בלשון אכילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:1.english: These words - [apply] where the verse expresses a prohibition of deriving benefit using the language of eating:

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:2.hebrew: היכא דנפיק לן אכילה והנאה מלא יאכל - אגב דמורי לן נמי אאכילה, מפיק ליה בלשון אכילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:2.english: Where [both] eating and benefit are derived for us from "it shall not be eaten" - Since it also teaches us regarding eating, [the verse] expresses it in the language of eating.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:3.hebrew: אבל הכא דאכילה נפקא לן מסקול יסקל - אי להנאה גרידתא אתא, לכתוב לא יהנה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:3.english: But here, where [the prohibition of] eating is derived for us from "it shall surely be stoned" - If it comes solely for [prohibiting] benefit, let [Scripture] write "benefit shall not be derived [from it]."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:4.english: Alternatively - Even according to you, let [the verse] write "It shall not be eaten," and nothing more.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:5.hebrew: את בשרו למה לי - אלא לאו לאשמועינן אע"ג דעבדיה כעין בשר שחוטה בהכשר, אסור באכילה ובהנאה, דהשתא אצטריך ליה לקרא לאפוקי בלשון אכילה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:23:5.english: Why do I [need] "its flesh" - Rather, [is it] not to teach us [that] even though he rendered it like properly slaughtered meat, it is prohibited for eating and for benefit? For now it was necessary for the verse to express it using the language of eating.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:24:1.hebrew: אימא ה"מ - דאסור אם שחטו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:24:1.english: Say this statement - that [it] is forbidden if he slaughtered it.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:3:1.hebrew: בחצר הניזק - דאילו ברה"ר, אין חייב ברגל לדברי הכל, דכתיב "בשדה אחר", בפ' קמא (דף ג:):
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:3:1.english: In the courtyard of the injured [party] - For in the public domain, [one] is not liable for [damage caused by] foot according to all opinions, as it is written, "in another's field," in the first chapter (3b).

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:3:2.hebrew: לאביי משלם כופר - אע"פ שלא נתכוון להזיק, דהא אוקי דרבעה ולא קטלה, הא קטלה משלם כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:3:2.english: According to Abaye, he pays ransom - Even though [the animal] did not intend to cause injury, for [Abaye] established [the earlier case as one] where it engaged in bestiality with her and did not kill her, [implying that] had it killed her, [the owner] would pay ransom.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:5:1.english: And both this and that are liable to death - For regarding an innocuous [ox] as well, it is written: "it shall surely be stoned."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:5:2.hebrew: וכן בבן וכן בבת - בן קטן ותינוקת קטנה, חייב עליהן סקילה וכופר כגדולים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:5:2.english: And the same [applies] to a son, and the same to a daughter - [Referring to] a minor boy and a minor girl; [one is] liable for them for stoning and ransom, just like [for] adults.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:7:1.hebrew: שאמדוהו לשלשה בני אדם - שרץ אחריהן זה אחר זה וברחו מפניו, ואמדו שאם לא ברחו, היה הורגן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:7:1.english: Where they assessed it [regarding] three people - That [the ox] ran after them one after another and they fled from it, and [the court] assessed that had they not fled, it would have killed them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:8:1.hebrew: שסיכן ג' בני אדם - לפיכך לא נסקל בשנים הראשונים, וכשנגח שלישי מתו כולם. הלכך, משלם עליו כופר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 41a:8:1.english: That it endangered three people - Therefore, it was not stoned for the first two, and when it gored [the] third, they all died. Therefore, [the owner] pays ransom for it.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:17:1.hebrew: איני יודע שהיא נבילה - וא"ת: אצטריך לבן פקועה לרבנן דרבי מאיר דלא בעי שחיטה (חולין דף עד.); וכ"ת דלא אקרי שור — הא לענין פטר חמור מקרי שה בפ"ק דבכורות (דף יב.) ובפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף עד:), ואפילו שחוט מוכח ביומא (דף מט: נ.) דמקרי פר, וכ"ש בן פקועה. וי"ל: בלאו הכי פריך שפיר; ולפי המסקנא ניחא, דנפקא לן מבשרו — אע"ג דשחטיה ועבדיה כעין בשר:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:17:1.english: Don't I know that it is an animal carcass - And if you should ask: [The verse] is needed for a ben pekua [a live fetus found inside a slaughtered animal] according to the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Meir, who hold that it does not require slaughter (Chullin 74a); and if you should say that it is not called an "ox" — behold, regarding the firstborn of a donkey, it is called a "lamb" in the first chapter of Bekhorot (12a) and in the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMaksheh (Chullin 74b), and even a slaughtered [animal] is proven in Yoma (49b–50a) to be called a "bull," and all the more so a ben pekua. And one can answer: Even without this, [the Baraita] asks well; and according to the conclusion, it is resolved, since we derive it from "its flesh" — even though he slaughtered it and rendered it like [kosher] flesh.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:1:1.hebrew: כמאן דקטלה דמי - וא"ת: ומה פשע השור? היא הרגה עצמה, שהרי הביאתו עליה! וי"ל, כמו שפירש ר"ח, שקפץ עליה השור לרבעה, ואלבשה בה יצרה ונתרצה. ואפילו למ"ד בכתובות פ' נערה (כתובות דף נא:) "תחילתה באונס וסופה ברצון" דמותר — היינו תחילת ביאה באונס; אבל הכא תחילת ביאה זו ברצון, ואסורה לכ"ע, וה"ה שנהרגה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:1:1.english: "Like one that killed her" - And if you ask: What fault did the ox have? She killed herself, for she brought it upon herself! One can answer, as Rabbeinu Chananel explained, that the ox leaped upon her to engage in bestiality with her, and her [evil] inclination took hold of her and she consented. And even according to the one who says in Ketubot, in the chapter [entitled] Na'arah (Ketubot 51b), [that when] "its beginning was under coercion and its end was with consent" she is permitted [to her husband] — that is [where] the beginning of the intercourse was under coercion; here, however, the beginning of this intercourse was with consent, and she is forbidden [to her husband] according to everyone, and the same applies that she is executed:

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:20:1.hebrew: והאי לא יאכל להיכא דסקליה מסקל דאסור בהנאה - ובעל השור נקי — להנאת עורו. וכי תימא: לשתוק מלא יאכל? אם כן, לא הוה מוקמינן נקי אלא להנאת בשר דוקא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:20:1.english: And this [phrase,] "shall not be eaten," [serves] for [a case] where they stoned it, [teaching] that it is prohibited from benefit - And [the phrase] "and the owner of the ox shall be clear" [comes] for the benefit of its hide. And if you say: Let [Scripture] be silent from [writing] "shall not be eaten"? If so, we would only establish "shall be clear" for the benefit of the flesh specifically.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:20:2.hebrew: כדרבי אבהו - לרווחא דמלתא נקט, דבלאו רבי אבהו לא הוה מצי למימר אלא להנאה, דלאכילה לא צריך:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:20:2.english: "In accordance with Rabbi Abbahu" - [The Gemara] mentions this for extra measure, for even without [the principle of] Rabbi Abbahu one could only say [that the verse comes] to [prohibit] benefit, since for [prohibiting] eating it is not needed.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:21:1.hebrew: כל מקום שנאמר לא יאכל - ואם תאמר: חמץ בפסח הנאתו יהיה בכרת, דכתיב "כי כל אוכל חמץ ונכרתה"? וכ"ת הכי נמי — א"כ, בפרק כל שעה (פסחים דף כג:) דבעי "מאי איכא בין חזקיה לרבי אבהו", הוה ליה למימר דהא איכא בינייהו! וי"ל: ד"לא יאכל" או "לא תאכל" ילפינן מ"לא תאכלו", אבל "כי כל אוכל" מ"לא תאכלו" לא ילפינן:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:21:1.english: Wherever it is stated: "It shall not be eaten" - And if you will ask: [Deriving] benefit from leavened bread (chametz) on Passover should be [punishable] by excision (karet), as it is written: "For whoever eats leavened bread [shall be] cut off"? And if you will say [that] indeed it is so — if so, in the chapter Kol Sha'ah (Pesachim 23b), where [the Gemara] asks: "What is [the difference] between Chizkiyah and Rabbi Abbahu?", it should have said that this is [a difference] between them! And one can answer: that "it shall not be eaten" (lo ye'akhel) or "you shall not eat" (lo tokhal) we derive from "you shall not eat" (lo tokhlu), but "for whoever eats" (ki khol okhel) we do not derive from "you shall not eat" (lo tokhlu).

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:2:1.hebrew: הא אין כוונתו להזיק - ואע"ג דכשכשה באמתה מבעיא בפ' כיצד הרגל (לעיל בבא קמא דף יט:), לפי שיש שם שינוי קצת ודמי טפי לקרן; אבל רביעה לאו שינוי הוא ולא דמי לקרן, וכשן גמורה היא שמזקת ע"י אכילה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:2:1.english: [In] this [case], its intention is not to cause injury - And even though [regarding a case where an animal] wagged its tail [and caused damage], [the Gemara] raises a question in the chapter [entitled] Keitzad HaRegel (above, Bava Kamma 19b), [that is] because there is a slight deviation there and it is more similar to keren [horn]; however, bestiality is not a deviation and is not similar to keren, and it is like full-fledged shen [tooth], which causes damage through eating.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:3:1.hebrew: ברגל שדרסה - שן הוה שייך למנקט הכא, אלא אגב דנקט רגל ספ"ב (דף כו.), נקטיה הכא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:3:1.english: With [an ox's] foot that trampled - It would have been appropriate to mention shen [damage by tooth] here; rather, since [the Gemara] mentioned regel [foot] at the end of the second chapter (26a), it mentioned it here [as well].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:3:2.hebrew: לרבא לא משלם כופר - אליבא דהך ברייתא קאמר, כדפי' בספ"ב (דף כו.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:3:2.english: According to Rava, he does not pay ransom - He states [this] according to this baraita, as explained at the end of the second chapter (26a):

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:6:1.hebrew: מאחר דמתם קטלינן כו' - לא מצי לאוקמי כגון שבשלש נגיחות ראשונות נתכוון להרוג הבהמה והרג את האדם, דכה"ג לא הוי מועד לאדם הואיל ולא נתכוון לאדם. וגם בהרג ג' פעמים על פני בעליו לא הוי מועד, כדאמרינן בפרק שני (דף כד.): אין השור נעשה מועד עד שיעידו בו בפני בעלים ובפני ב"ד:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:6:1.english: [But] since we kill [it] when it is innocuous, etc. - [The Gemara] cannot establish [the case] as [one] where during the first three gorings it intended to kill an animal and killed a person, for in such a case it does not become forewarned (mu'ad) with respect to a person, since it did not intend [to kill] a person. And also, if it killed three times in the presence of its owner, it does not become forewarned, as we say in the second chapter (24a): "An ox does not become forewarned until they testify about it in the presence of the owner and in the presence of a court."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:7:1.hebrew: כגון שאמדוהו לג' בני אדם - כולה סוגיא מוכחא דלא מיחייב בשלישי נ"ש, כדפרישית בפ"ב (דף כד.):
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 41a:7:1.english: For example, where they assessed it for three people - The entire sugya proves that [the owner] is not liable for full damages on the third [time], as I explained in the second chapter (24a).
